chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
He (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of women is not valid regarding the new moon, nor regarding divorce.'
And he (the narrator) said: 'I asked him (peace be upon him) about women, is their testimony valid?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, regarding virginity and the postpartum period.'
ai.seo_question: When is the testimony of women considered valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi delineates the juristic boundaries of female testimony, restricting it in public or legal domains like lunar sighting and divorce while validating it in private, bodily matters such as virginity and postpartum status. This distinction reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the context of expertise and privacy, aligning with the principle that women's testimony is accepted where their specific experience or observation is most reliable.
